title: Why do ads seem to follow you around the internet?

lines.text: Why does that pair of sneakers you looked at once on Amazon follow you onto Instagram, YouTube, and news sites?
lines.caps: Why does that one *ad | follow you everywhere *online?

lines.text: This marketing tactic is called retargeting, and it is powered by an invisible bidding auction.
lines.caps: It's called *retargeting | powered by instant ad *auctions!

lines.text: When you browse a product, the website drops a tracking pixel or first-party cookie in your browser.
lines.caps: The site drops an *invisible | tracking pixel in your *browser

lines.text: This pixel tags your browser with a unique anonymous user identifier.
lines.caps: Tags your device with a *unique | anonymous *identity

lines.text: Whenever you visit an entirely different website, ad exchange networks recognize your tracking ID.
In milliseconds, automated algorithms conduct a lightning auction, selling that ad banner to the sneaker brand for pennies.
lines.caps: Automated auctions sell the *banner | to the sneaker store in *milliseconds!

lines.text: Clear your browser cache and cookies regularly to shake off the ad trackers following you.
lines.caps: Clear cookies to *shake off | the digital *trackers!
